summary.headline: Adani Green FY26 power supply revenue rose 22% to INR11,602 crore, with 5.1 GW added and operating capacity at 19.3 GW.
summary.overview: Management presented FY26 results on a fixed-income investor call: energy sales up 34% YoY to 37.6 billion units, and 5.1 GW of capacity added (35% YoY) taking operating portfolio to 19.3 GW. Revenue from power supply rose 22% to INR11,602 crore and EBITDA grew 23% to INR10,865 crore, a 91.2% margin. Management said FY27 greenfield additions will be 4.5-5.0 GW, sized to evacuation availability, with battery storage targeted to reach 10 GWh in Khavda by year-end. The call was brief and the Q&A covered only capex, battery plans and funding; the funding answer was not provided in the transcript.

segments.name: Solar, wind and hybrid (Khavda and group)
segments.commentary: About 9.4 GW of solar, wind and hybrid assets in operations at Khavda, including group capacities. FY26 added 5.1 GW, described as the highest greenfield annual capacity extension globally by any company outside China.

segments.name: Battery energy storage
segments.commentary: About 3 GWh close to operation at Khavda, with 1.4 GWh added in the year. Target is 10 GWh by end of FY27 at a similar pace.

segments.name: Pumped hydro storage
segments.commentary: Maiden 500 MW project at Chitravathi, Andhra Pradesh, slated for completion in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 solar and wind capacity addition planned at 4.5-5.0 GW, aligned to evacuation capacity coming up in the year, below the 5 GW+ the company says it can build.
Battery storage target of 10 GWh in Khavda by end of this year (FY27).
500 MW Chitravathi pumped hydro project to be completed in FY27.
Long-term target of 50 GW by 2030 reaffirmed; company intends to keep similar greenfield addition pace going forward.
capex_capacity: FY27 solar/wind/hybrid additions planned at 4.5-5.0 GW, gated by evacuation (transmission) availability and offtake.
Management says it has shown capability for 5 GW+ annual additions and will go further if evacuation and opportunities allow.
Battery storage at Khavda near 3 GWh; plan to reach 10 GWh by year-end.
Pumped hydro 500 MW at Chitravathi, Andhra Pradesh, due this fiscal year.
Total operating portfolio 19.3 GW, enough to power 8.7 million homes and avoid about 36 million tonnes of CO2 annually.
demand_pricing: Energy sales growth of 34% in FY26 was attributed to greenfield additions and strong operating performance at each plant.
Management cited India's record FY26 non-fossil capacity addition of over 55 GW and about 283 GW installed non-fossil capacity, against a 500 GW 2030 goal.
No pricing, tariff or order-book details were discussed in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 greenfield capacity and Khavda battery plans, and what is the funding plan including average cost of debt and maturity?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery storage is near 3 GWh and will reach 10 GWh by end of this year. Solar and wind additions are planned at 4.5-5.0 GW, matched to evacuation capacity, though the company could add 5 GW+. The funding, cost of debt and maturity parts of the question were not answered in the transcript.

risks_watch: Evacuation and transmission constraints are the stated limit on FY27 capacity additions (4.5-5.0 GW).
Funding details (average cost of debt, debt maturity profile, capex quantum) were requested but not disclosed in this call; check the debt investor materials.
Execution on 10 GWh battery storage target and 500 MW Chitravathi pumped hydro in FY27.
Revenue growth (22%) is below energy sales growth (34%), which suggests lower realisation per unit; the call gave no explanation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on operating scale, ESG and rating milestones. Cautious on FY27 additions, which management tied explicitly to evacuation constraints. Evasive on the funding and cost-of-debt question, which went unanswered.
key_quotes: This is the highest greenfield annual capacity extension globally by any company outside China.
we are currently planning to add 4.5 to 5.0 gigawatt of our solar and wind capacity.
Our plan is to add in the same rate and by the end of this year to add 10 gigawatt hour of storage capacities in Khavda.
